editorial:
Imagine you are a reporter in post-war Germany, just trying to do your job, when you find out a luxury yacht sank for no apparent reason. That is exactly where you start with Peter Zabel. He is curious and stubborn, and he cannot shake the feeling that a wedding party of artists didn't just vanish into the ocean by accident. The whole movie feels like a rainy night in a big city, full of shadows and secrets. You will feel like you are walking right beside Zabel as he digs into the mystery, wondering if the government or some sneaky political group is hiding the truth about what really happened on that ship.

What really works here is how the movie keeps you guessing. The acting is solid and the slow build-up makes the reveals feel earned. It does move a bit slower than modern thrillers, but the mood makes up for it. If you love old-school detective stories, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a quiet weekend night.
endingExplained: You find out that the sinking was not an accident or a political plot, but a tragic mistake involving personal secrets. Zabel discovers that the ship went down because of a struggle on board that led to a leak. The truth comes out through witnesses who were too scared to talk at first. In the end, the mystery is solved, but it leaves you feeling sad because the loss of life was totally avoidable.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old detective mysteries and film noir.
